messages.content: my family would like to watch a film this evening. how can we choose one?
ask each person what kind of film they would like to watch. then try to choose one that you can all enjoy.
there are only two of us, and we would like to watch a short film.
you could each choose a short film. then ask each other which one to watch first.
what if we each want to watch our own one first?
you could watch one first today and let the other person choose first next time.
help me write about my friend who works in a store.
my friend works in a store. she helps people find things and keeps the store clean.
make it about two friends.
my friends work in a store. they help people find things and keep the store clean.
why did you change works to work?
use works with she or he. use work with they.
can you give me another example?
she cleans the store. they clean the store.
i want to ask my neighbor to help move a big chair.
could you help me move this chair, please?
say it is going from the living room to the bedroom.
could you help me move this chair from the living room to the bedroom, please?
i do not want them to think they have to do it all alone.
could you help me move this chair from the living room to the bedroom? i can help carry it with you.
write a talk at a store about buying a blue shirt. do not add a price.

worker: hello. can i help you? woman: yes. i am looking for a blue shirt. worker: what size would you like? woman: a small one, please. worker: here is a small blue shirt. woman: thank you. can i see how it looks? worker: yes. there is a mirror over there. woman: i like the color. do you have the same shirt in green? worker: yes, i can bring one. woman: thank you. i would like to look at both before i choose.
did she buy the blue one for sure?
no. she would like to look at both before choosing.
my cousin is coming to stay. what should i put in the bedroom?
you could put a clean blanket and pillow on the bed, and leave a clean towel where your cousin can find it.
write a short list with just these things.
clean blanket, pillow, clean towel.
should i ask if the room is warm enough?
yes. you could say: is the room warm enough, or would you like another blanket?
write one sentence about a cold glass of water on a warm day.
the cold glass of water felt good in her hand on the warm afternoon.
did you feel that?
no. that is a sentence about a person in a story. i do not have hands or feel a glass of water.
can you write another sentence about what she did next?
she sat by the window and drank the water before going outside again.
write about my brother watching birds every morning.
my brother watches birds every morning. he stands by the window and looks at the tree outside.
now make it yesterday.
my brother watched birds yesterday morning. he stood by the window and looked at the tree outside.
can you make the first one about my parents?
my parents watch birds every morning. they stand by the window and look at the tree outside.
i can give my friend my book today, but i want it back.
you could say: you can have my book today. please bring it back when you finish reading it.
i need it back tomorrow, even if they do not finish.
you can have my book today, but please bring it back tomorrow. i need it then.
make it sound kind.
you are welcome to read my book today. could you please bring it back tomorrow? i need it then.
help me write about a trip i would like to take by plane.
i would like to take a trip by plane and see a new country. i would look out of the window and watch the earth below.
i have never been on a plane. does that sentence say i have?
no. it says you would like to take the trip. it does not say you already took it.
add that i would go with my sister.
i would like to take a trip by plane with my sister and see a new country.
my friend is quiet today. i think she may feel sad.
you could ask how she is feeling and let her choose if she would like to talk.
write what i can say.
you seem quiet today. would you like to talk, or would you like some quiet time?
what if she says she just feels tired?
you can listen to what she says. you could say: okay. would you like to rest for a while?
tell me a short story about a student learning a song.

a student studied a song at home. at first, she could not remember all the words. she read one line, then tried to sing it. she did the same with the next line. after a while, she learned the first part of the song. she started to sing it to her sister, who listened from the sofa. her sister asked to hear it again. the student was happy to sing it once more before learning the next part.
did she learn all the song at once?
no. she learned it one part at a time.
a man is standing outside a hospital. is he a doctor?
he could be, but standing outside a hospital does not tell us his work. he could be visiting someone or waiting for a friend.
he has a bag too.
having a bag still does not tell us if he is a doctor.
so we cannot be sure?
right. we cannot be sure about his work just from where he is standing and what he is carrying.
then what do we know?
only what you said: a man with a bag is standing outside a hospital.
write about a bird sleeping in a tree.
a little bird sleeps in the tree near my window.
now say what it is doing right now.
a little bird is sleeping in the tree near my window.
make it about yesterday instead.
a little bird slept in the tree near my window yesterday.
does slept tell us it is sleeping now?
no. it is about a time before now.
my friend speaks in a very quiet voice and i cannot hear. how can i ask them to speak up?
could you speak up a little, please? i cannot hear you well.
make it shorter.
could you speak up, please?
do i have to say they are doing it wrong?
no. you can just say what you need. could you speak up a little, please is enough.
make a sentence with carries and arms.
she carries the baby in her arms.
now use carried.
she carried the baby in her arms.
are they her arms or the arms of the baby?
they are the arms of the person carrying the baby.
does that say the baby can walk?
no. the sentence only says she carried the baby. it does not tell us if the baby can walk.
should i choose a banana or an apple?
which fruit do you feel like eating? you can choose the one you would enjoy now.
i like both, but i had a banana this morning.
then you could choose an apple now if you would like a change.
yes, i would like an apple now.
then choose an apple. you can like both, but you do not have to eat both at once.
i am making lunch for a friend. i have chicken, rice, and beans.
you could make chicken with rice and beans. does your friend eat chicken?
no. they do not eat meat.
then leave out the chicken. you could make rice with beans for your friend.
should i ask if they like beans first?
yes. you could say: would you like rice with beans for lunch?
keep the answer short. what do i leave out?
the chicken.
give me a sentence with sends.
she sends a letter to her brother every year.
now use sent.
she sent a letter to her brother yesterday.
another one with sends, but not about a letter.
he sends a photo to his mother when he visits a new place.
change he to they.
they send a photo to their mother when they visit a new place.
my flower has a yellow leaf. is it not well?
one yellow leaf alone may not tell you that. do you know what kind of flower it is and how much water it gets?
i only know it is by the window.
i cannot tell from that alone. you could ask someone who knows about that kind of flower and show them the leaf.
so you do not know for sure?
right. i do not know for sure from what you have said.
that is all i need for today.
okay. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
thank you for keeping it simple.
you are welcome.
i will come back tomorrow if i need more help.
you can open this webpage again when you would like to talk.
you do not need to give me another thing to do.
okay. goodbye for now.
